metadata.summary: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have mapped thousands of congenital heart disease (CHD)-associated variants within non-coding regions of the genome. Non-coding variants can alter regulatory mechanisms, such as transcription factor (TF) binding control of gene expression, potentially contributing human diseases. However, with the increasing number of disease-associated variants, comprehensive functional validation remains a significant challenge. In this work, we developed a novel method called SNP Bind-n-Seq to evaluate >3,000 CHD-risk variants for allelic binding for the cardiac TFs NKX2-5, GATA4, and TBX5 in a high-throughput manner. These binding affinity data sets were coupled with a massively parallel reporter assay (MPRA) to screen CHD-risk variant genotype-dependent regulatory activity. We identified 170 variants that exhibit allelic TF binding and 187 that modulate gene expression. Combining both approaches revealed three high-confidence variants with genotype-dependent TF binding, genotype-dependent transcriptional activity, and eQTL behavior in cardiac cells. Collectively, this study provides the first combined high-throughput biochemical and functional genomic evaluation of thousands of CHD-risk variants.

metadata.summary: Background. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress. Our goal was to determine the effects of the dual SGLT1 and SGLT2 inhibitor sotagliflozin (SOTA) on myocardial remodeling, diastolic function, mitochondrial gene expression and oxidative stress in mice with HCM due to the tropomyosin E180G mutation (E180G). Methods. Male E180G and non-carrier (NC) mice 7-8 weeks old were randomized to SOTA formulated in the chow (30 mg/kg chow) or control diet (CD) for 8 weeks. Cardiac structure and function were assessed by echocardiography at baseline, and after 4 and 8 weeks of treatment. At 8 weeks mice were sacrificed to assess myocardial histology, RNA expression, oxidative stress and oxidative sulfonylation of sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium ATPase (SERCA). Results. At baseline E180G mice had myocardial hypertrophy, interstitial fibrosis, diastolic dysfunction and atrial enlargement - all of which worsened over the next 8 weeks. In E180G mice treatment with SOTA for 8 weeks prevented further LV hypertrophy and atrial enlargement, decreased interstitial fibrosis and normalized diastolic function. Mitochondrial gene sets were downregulated, and oxidative stress was increased and associated with oxidative sulfonylation of SERCA at C674. SOTA treatment upregulated mitochondrial gene sets and prevented the increases in oxidative stress and SERCA oxidation. Upregulated fibrosis gene sets in E180G hearts were not affected by SOTA. Conclusion. In E180G HCM mice downregulation of mitochondrial gene sets is associated with increased oxidative stress and oxidative modification of SERCA. In E180G hearts, SOTA corrected the HCM phenotype, normalized diastolic function, upregulated mitochondrial gene sets, and decreased oxidative stress and SERCA oxidation. Upregulation of mitochondrial gene sets leading to improved mitochondrial function may improve energetics and decrease oxidative stress. Oxidative stress leads to oxidative modification of SERCA and stimulation of fibrosis pathways which may play a significant role in HCM, and thus provide an opportunity for therapeutic intervention with agents that improve mitochondrial function and/or decrease oxidative stress.

observations.title: Dual SGLT1 and 2 inhibition with sotagliflozin decreases oxidative stress in mice with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy due to tropomyosin E180G mutation

metadata.summary: Epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) exhibit limited efficacy against lung cancer brain metastases, often resulting in rapid and inevitable resistance. However, the unique mechanisms driving this brain microenvironment-specific therapeutic failure remain elusive. Here, utilizing in vivo orthotopic models and single-cell RNA sequencing, we reveal that targeted therapy induces a distinct, metabolically hyperactive senescent cell subpopulation that drives rapid EGFR-TKI tolerance in brain metastasis. We identify the molecular chaperone CRYAB as an indispensable driver specifically upregulated within this senescent persister state. Mechanistically, CRYAB physically interacts with VDAC2 at the outer mitochondrial membrane, promoting endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-mitochondria tethering and calcium influx. This CRYAB-VDAC2 axis orchestrates adaptive mitochondrial fission, hyperactivating oxidative metabolism while simultaneously shielding（preventing？） senescent cells from fatal oxidative stress. Genetic or pharmacological blockade of mitochondrial fission completely abolishes CRYAB-mediated therapeutic resistance. Therapeutically, we demonstrate that a 25-hydroxycholesterol (25HC) dietary intervention acts as a potent in vivo senolytic strategy, directly dismantling the CRYAB-dependent resistance network, eradicating senescent persister cells, and synergistically prolonging overall survival when combined with Osi. Furthermore, high baseline CRYAB expression in pre-treatment primary lung biopsies clinically predicts lower intracranial objective response rates and shorter progression-free survival in a cohort of advanced EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients. Collectively, our study uncovers a novel CRYAB-VDAC2-mitochondrial fission axis that enforces therapy-induced senescence and highlights 25HC dietary intervention as a highly translatable combinatorial strategy to overcome EGFR-TKI resistance in brain metastasis.

observations.title: CRYAB-driven mitochondrial fission induces senescence to promote adaptive resistance to EGFR-TKI in LUAD brain metastasis

metadata.summary: Tumor heterogeneity arises from the sequential acquisition of somatic mutations and the selection of fitter clones, leading to distinct genotypes and phenotypes. Joint mapping of genome and transcriptome in the same tumor tissue can directly link clonoal relation to transcriptional state enabling a more in-depth understanding of intrinsic and extrinct tumor heterogeneity in the tissue context. Here, we introduce Spatial-GT-seq, a spatial multi-omic technology capable of genome-wide co-profiling of the genome and transcriptome at near single-cell resolution. We demonstrated in situ identification of tumor subclones in a mouse model of lung metastasis, with parallel transcriptomic profiles indicating that the gene expression profile of the same tumor clone is altered by the tumor microenvironment. Furthermore, analysis of primary and recurrent human pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors reveals both persistent and newly emerging tumor subclones, exhibiting transcriptional changes in both the original and recurrence sites. These findings highlight Spatial-GT-seq as a valuable platform for studying genotype-phenotype-microenvironment associations, providing new insights into cancer evolution and heterogeneity.

observations.title: Spatial genome and transcriptome co-mapping reveals clonal heterogeneity in tumor tissue [RNA-Seq]

observations.text:
BackgroundThe nonfluent/agrammatic (nfv) and logopenic (lv) variants of primary progressive aphasia (PPA) disrupt fluency through distinct underlying neurocognitive mechanisms. Differential diagnosis currently requires hours of cognitive-linguistic testing, with additional barriers for bilingual patients due to a shortage of bilingual service providers and a lack of well-established assessment methods. In English speakers, a promising automated approach for differentiating nfvPPA and lvPPA is to derive speech-timing measures and linguistic features from connected speech as input to machine learning (ML) classification algorithms. To our knowledge, this approach has not been evaluated in the context of bilingualism.

MethodsThirty-four Catalan-Spanish simultaneous bilingual patients (lv = 24, nfv = 10) were asked to describe a picture (Western Aphasia Battery Picnic Scene) in both their dominant and non- dominant language. From the participants recorded response, we derived four feature sets: speech-timing measures, derived with PRAAT; word-level parameters, derived from corpora; linguistic features, derived with the natural language processing tools SpaCy and CLAN; image-text congruence scores, derived with the vision-language encoder Multilingual-CLIP. Each feature set was fed into classification algorithms for differentiating nfv from lv in participants non-dominant and dominant samples. Then, we combined each feature sets classifier into an ensemble model. We used the McNemar test to determine the statistical significance of differences in classification performance between responses in the non-dominant and dominant language.

ResultsThe best-performing classifier achieved F1 macro scores of 93% (word-level parameters) and 92% (ensemble) in the non-dominant and dominant language, respectively. For all feature sets and ensemble models, classification performance did not significantly differ between the non-dominant and dominant language. Ensemble modeling did not significantly improve classification performance in either language.

ConclusionsTaking advantage of recent advances in multilingual multimodal machine learning, we accurately differentiate Spanish-Catalan bilingual individuals with nfvPPA and lvPPA using a largely automated, time-efficient (1-2 minutes), and ecologically valid connected-speech-based approach. Future directions include evaluating this approach on larger datasets balanced by PPA subtype, using automated transcriptions of connected speech. Our study represents a step towards addressing current inequities in PPA differential diagnosis for non-English-speaking bilingual speakers.

Trial registrationData from the clinical trial NCT05741853 was retrospectively analyzed
observations.title: Differentiating nonfluent/agrammatic and logopenic primary progressive aphasia in Catalan-Spanish bilinguals by applying multilingual multimodal machine learning to connected speech

metadata.summary: Aims: Sinoatrial node (SAN) dysfunction is commonly observed in obesity and diabetes and is associated with increased cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Cardiac steatosis, characterized by excessive intracellular lipid droplet (LD) accumulation in cardiomyocytes, is common in these metabolic disorders, but its direct contribution to SAN dysfunction remains unclear. We investigated whether intracellular LD accumulation impairs SAN automaticity. Methods and Results: Transgenic mice (TG) with cardiomyocyte-specific overexpression of perilipin 2 (PLIN2) and double-transgenic mice (DTG) co-expressing PLIN2 and hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL) were studied. TG mice exhibited marked LD accumulation in SAN myocytes together with prolonged and highly variable R–R intervals on electrocardiography (ECG). Optical Ca²⁺ mapping of SAN–atrial preparations demonstrated displacement of the leading pacemaker site toward peripheral nodal and extranodal regions in TG mice. Isolated TG SAN myocytes exhibited reduced sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca²⁺ content, attenuated local Ca²⁺ releases (LCRs), and elevated intracellular and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels. In contrast, mitochondrial and SR ultrastructure were unaltered, and global gene expression profiles were preserved, except for PLIN2 overexpression. Normalization of intracellular LD accumulation by HSL co-expression prevented abnormalities in ECG, SAN automaticity, intracellular Ca²⁺ handling, and ROS levels despite persistent PLIN2 overexpression. This study was limited by the use of male mice, and the causal contribution of elevated ROS to the observed SAN dysfunction was not directly tested. Conclusion: Intracellular LD accumulation alone was sufficient to alter intracellular Ca²⁺ handling and impair SAN automaticity. Normalization of intracellular LD accumulation by HSL co-expression prevented SAN dysfunction, supporting a causal role for intracellular LD accumulation in pacemaker dysfunction. These findings identify myocardial steatosis as a previously underrecognized contributor to SAN dysfunction.

observations.title: Excess accumulation of intracellular lipid droplet impairs sinoatrial function in a mouse model of myocardial steatosis

metadata.summary: Nutraceuticals such as (+)-Catechin are emerging as promising agents for the prevention and treatment of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. A large prospective study of 34,492 participants previously demonstrated an inverse association between (+)-Catechin intake and risk for coronary heart disease. Our recent work further showed that (+)-Catechin inhibits several atherosclerosis related processes in vitro, induces beneficial metabolic changes in male C57BL/6J mice fed a high fat diet (HFD), and reduces plaque burden and inflammation in male low-density lipoprotein (LDL) receptor deficient (LDLr / ) mice fed a HFD. Given known sex specific differences in atherosclerosis, it is essential to extend these investigations to female mice. The objective of this study was therefore to investigate the effects of (+)-Catechin in female LDLr /  mice in vivo. (+)-Catechin lowered plasma cholesterol levels, reduced circulating T cell populations, and increased several beneficial short chain fatty acids in both the plasma and the faeces. It also decreased plaque size, lipid content, macrophage accumulation, and CD3⁺ T cell infiltration in the aortic root, while enhancing markers of plaque stability. RNA sequencing (RNA seq) of the thoracic aorta revealed modulation of key pathways involved in inflammatory signalling, hypertension and immune responses. Complementary studies in human aortic smooth muscle cells demonstrated that (+)-Catechin attenuated macropinocytosis and oxidised LDL uptake, processes linked to plaque progression, without promoting calcification. RNA seq identified several genes and pathways consistent with the compound’s anti atherogenic and plaque stabilising actions. Collectively, these findings provide new mechanistic insights into the beneficial cardiovascular effects of (+)-Catechin in female mice and support further evaluation of this flavanol in human clinical trials.

observations.text:
BackgroundQuality Control Circle (QCC) reports are often reviewed qualitatively, but reviewer workload and inter-rater variability make large-scale assessment difficult. We evaluated whether multiple large language models (LLMs) could score QCC methodological quality reliably on a designed-anchor benchmark.

ObjectiveTo estimate inter-model reliability for QCC quality scoring and to assess alignment with designed anchors and descriptive comparability to a small set of public PMC QCC reports.

MethodsThirty synthetic QCC reports and eight public PMC QCC reports were evaluated across four primary LLM evaluators (GPT, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek) and one sensitivity evaluator (Claude); Claude was excluded from the primary panel because a same-family model generated the synthetic cases. Evaluators received the report text only; the trap manifest and designed-anchor scores were withheld, and their absence was verified programmatically. Each case was scored on eight QCC quality dimensions in three runs per evaluator, summarized by median, and ICC(A,1) was estimated across the primary panel. Anchor calibration, trap detection from the evaluators structured defect output under a map fixed before scoring, sensitivity analyses, and a descriptive synthetic-versus-PMC check were also examined.

ResultsInter-model reliability on the primary k=4 panel was good: ICC(A,1) = 0.843 (95% CI 0.812 to 0.870; case-level bootstrap 0.782 to 0.874) on 239 pooled case-dimension rows from all 30 cases; per-dimension estimates ranged from 0.747 to 0.901. The pre-specified k=5 analysis including Claude gave 0.833, leave-one-out estimates ranged from 0.835 to 0.857, and the originally specified score parser gave 0.854. On the 52 trap-affected case-dimension cells the primary-panel consensus fell within {+/-}1 of the designed anchor in 50 (96.2%), with mean absolute error 0.54 and exact agreement 34.6%; 51.5% of individual primary-panel run scores equalled the anchor. A defect of the expected category was emitted in 87% of evaluator runs and by 94% of (trap, evaluator) pairs, versus 55% and 68% for a pre-specified keyword detector; because some categories are emitted at high base rates regardless of case, these are upper bounds. All eight dimensions met the descriptive synthetic-versus-PMC margin; synthetic cases tended to score higher, significantly so only for Action Alignment.

ConclusionsMulti-model LLM scoring of QCC methodological quality achieved good inter-model reliability and directionally consistent alignment with synthetic anchor scores, with planted weaknesses identified far more often in structured defect output than by keyword matching. Benchmark feasibility is established; expert-labeled validation in clinical QCC reports is the planned next step.
observations.title: Multi-model LLM assessment of Quality Control Circle methodological quality: a designed-anchor reliability study

metadata.summary: Fibroblast differentiation into matrix-producing, contractile myofibroblasts is accompanied by metabolic reprogramming, but whether these changes precede differentiation or arise from the activated phenotype remains unclear. To define when transcriptional remodeling emerges after TGFβ stimulation, we performed bulk RNA-seq on cardiac fibroblasts treated with TGFβ or bFGF for 1, 6, 12, 24, or 48 h. Our transcripomics revealed only 394 genes were differentially expressed at 1 h, but 4,188 DEGs were detected by 6 h, with the total DEG burden peaking at 24 h. These findings support a phased, time-dependent remodeling of the cardiac fibroblast transcriptome in response to TGFβ relative to bFGF in which an initially limited response occurs at 1 h, expands substantially by 6 h, and subsequently encompasses cell cycle regulation, stress responses, developmental- and differentiation-associated programs, cell adhesion, and extracellular matrix remodeling.

observations.title: Time-resolved RNA-seq reveals a phased transcriptional response to TGFβ stimulation

observations.text: GABAergic inhibitory neurons play a central role in shaping network dynamics, and accordingly, their dysfunction is implicated in the pathophysiology of various psychiatric, neurodevelopmental, and neurological disorders. In the past decade, studies on vasoactive intestinal polypeptide-expressing inhibitory neurons (VIP+ neurons) have positioned them as critical components of this circuitry. In particular, VIP+ neurons have been proposed to function within a canonical disinhibitory circuit motif, preferentially inhibiting other interneuron subtypes, to ultimately modulate the gain and activity of local pyramidal neurons. However, their contribution to psychiatrically relevant behavioral endophenotypes is still not fully understood, limiting our ability to target these neurons for therapeutic purposes. In the present study, we systematically assessed the functional contribution of VIP+ neurons to affective and social behaviors. To this end, we used a chemogenetic approach to manipulate the activity of VIP+ neurons in core corticolimbic regions, including the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), basolateral amygdala (BLA), and ventral hippocampus (vHPC). The consequences of either activating or inhibiting VIP+ neurons in these regions were observed while mice underwent a battery of behavioral tasks assessing anxiety-related avoidance behaviors, social interest and recognition, and associative fear learning. While sustained modulation of VIP+ neurons had no significant effect on anxiety-related or social behaviors in any of the brain regions assessed, it produced a robust reduction in associative fear learning specifically in the mPFC. These findings demonstrate that the consequences of sustained VIP+ neuron modulation depend on both anatomical location and behavioural context. Moreover, they identify VIP+ neurons in the mPFC as potentially clinically relevant targets for interventions aimed at modulating fear-related circuits.
observations.title: Consequences of sustained modulation of VIP-expressing neurons in mouse corticolimbic regions on anxiety-related avoidance behaviors, social functioning, and associative fear learning

observations.text: Patients with majority variant subtype histology including sarcomatoid urothelial carcinoma (SUC) have poor outcomes and limited treatment options, and there are few preclinical resources to investigate rare histologic subtypes. We developed three novel variant subtype histology bladder cancer (BC) cell lines by finding that basal BC tumor cells derived from mice treated with N-butyl-N-(4-hydroxybutyl)-nitrosamine (BBN) were initially not competent to grow in immune competent mice, but then acquired tumorigenicity following passaging (recycling) in mice lacking mature B and T cells. Three genitourinary oncology pathologists identified BBN966 as SUC, BBN964 as a hybrid between SUC and squamous, and BBN975 as squamous, and each had unique growth characteristics. Using a publicly available dataset and our spatial transcriptomics analysis of a cohort of human tumors with mixed SUC and UC as comparators, we found that consistent with human SUC, BBN966 lack expression of basal and luminal genes. Consistent with human SUC and spatial transcriptomics analysis of canine SUC, BBN966 had the highest epithelial to mesenchymal transition (EMT) upregulation, and all three recycled tumor cells had increased EMT pathway expression in recycled tumor cells. Moreover, increased expression of genes upregulated in all three recycled tumor cells associated with worse overall survival in patients with muscle invasive UC. Similar to human SUC, BBN966 tumors had higher proportion of M2 macrophage gene expression. Finally, we found in the largest cohort of PD-L1 IHC to date that 20 of 38 (52.6%) human SUC had CPS > 50, which was driven mostly by tumor proportion score. Consistent with this, we found anti-PD1 immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) significantly inhibited BBN966 tumor growth, while the hybrid BBN964 tumors had mixed response to ICI. Thus, the murine BBN966 tumors exhibited similarities to human SUC, and can be used to examine novel therapies for translation into future SUC clinical studies.
observations.title: Epithelial to mesenchymal transition and M2 macrophages drive aggressiveness in murine and human sarcomatoid urothelial carcinoma.

observations.text: Epicardial activation is a conserved response to injury across vertebrates, yet only in regenerative species do epicardium-derived cells (EPDCs) acquire the capacity to invade the injury site and contribute to cardiac regeneration. How regenerative competence is established in epicardial cells downstream of activation remains poorly understood. Using multicolour lineage tracing we find that epicardial cells of the salamander species Pleurodeles waltl undergo a transient phase of clonal expansion that precedes EPDC accumulation at the injury site. Depletion of cCpE-sensitive Claudins from otherwise intact tight junctions alters the organisation and the mechanical state of the epicardium, impairs clonal expansion and reduces the capacity of epicardial cells to delaminate. Consequently, EPDCs fail to activate a regenerative transcriptional programme and complete their transition into injury-induced migratory EPDCs that are required to sculpt a Tenascin-C-rich matrix supporting cardiomyocyte protrusion at the injury site. Together, our findings demonstrate that epicardial activation alone is insufficient for regeneration and identify Claudin-dependent clonal expansion as a mechanism that couples epicardial activation to the acquisition of a regenerative EPDC state.
observations.title: Claudin-dependent clonal expansion couples epicardial activation to regenerative fate acquisition

metadata.summary: Tumor heterogeneity arises from the sequential acquisition of somatic mutations and the selection of fitter clones, leading to distinct genotypes and phenotypes. Joint mapping of genome and transcriptome in the same tumor tissue can directly link clonoal relation to transcriptional state enabling a more in-depth understanding of intrinsic and extrinct tumor heterogeneity in the tissue context. Here, we introduce Spatial-GT-seq, a spatial multi-omic technology capable of genome-wide co-profiling of the genome and transcriptome at near single-cell resolution. We demonstrated in situ identification of tumor subclones in a mouse model of lung metastasis, with parallel transcriptomic profiles indicating that the gene expression profile of the same tumor clone is altered by the tumor microenvironment. Furthermore, analysis of primary and recurrent human pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors reveals both persistent and newly emerging tumor subclones, exhibiting transcriptional changes in both the original and recurrence sites. These findings highlight Spatial-GT-seq as a valuable platform for studying genotype-phenotype-microenvironment associations, providing new insights into cancer evolution and heterogeneity.

metadata.summary: The prevalence of neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) is increasing, with growing evidence implicating the intrauterine environment as a critical regulator of fetal brain development. Gestational perturbations such as maternal stress can increase NDD risk; however, the mechanism(s) by which prenatal maternal stress reshape fetal neurodevelopment remain unclear. Accordingly, the objective of my project was to characterize how maternal cold stress exposure during pregnancy disrupts neural stem and progenitor cell (NSPC) developmental programs in the fetus and the impact this has on neurodevelopment in the hypothalamus. Pregnant mice were exposed to 4°C for 30 minutes daily from embryonic day 11.5 (E11.5) to E15.5—a critical period of neurodevelopment in the hypothalamus. To assess how maternal cold stress impacts neural stem cell (NSC) behaviours, we employed the neurosphere assay, quantifying the number and size of primary and secondary neurospheres as a measure of NSC proliferation and self-renewal, respectively. Our findings revealed no change in NSC proliferation or self-renewal when comparing control and maternal cold stress male and female neurospheres. However, differentiation of dissociated NSCs revealed that neurons from both sexes had longer axons following maternal cold stress exposure. Interestingly, only male-derived cultures exhibited a significant increase in the number TUJ1+ neurons in response to maternal cold stress exposure, whereas only female-derived maternal cold stress cultures showed enhanced dendritic arborization. To explore the molecular basis of these changes, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing on E15.5 fetal hypothalamic NSPCs. Analysis of differentially expressed genes uncovered basal sex differences between the transcriptional signatures of control male and female Cycling NSPCs and suggested that maternal cold stress shifts female Cycling NSPCs toward a more male-like transcriptional profile. Gene ontology analysis revealed that maternal cold stress upregulates pathways linked to neuronal growth, development, and GABAergic neuron differentiation, but only in females. Importantly, ligand-receptor analysis suggested that maternal cold stress exposure disrupts neurodevelopmental programs through altered cell-cell signalling within Cycling NSPCs predominantly in females. These findings demonstrate that prenatal maternal cold stress exposure drives sex-specific effects on fetal neurodevelopment and uncover distinct cellular pathways that may contribute to sex differences seen in the presentation and risk of many NDDs.

observations.title: Prenatal maternal cold stress exposure drives sex-specific neurodevelopmental disruptions in the fetal hypothalamus

observations.text:
BackgroundCardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome encompasses interconnected diseases that share pathophysiological mechanisms, including microvascular dysfunction. Although rubidium-82 positron emission tomography/computed tomography ({superscript 2}Rb-PET/CT) is routinely used for myocardial perfusion imaging, its potential for integrated cardio-renal perfusion assessment and broader CKM phenotyping remains underexplored. We recently developed a compartment modelling approach to quantify renal perfusion from existing routine cardiac 82Rb-PET/CT scans, enabling simultaneous assessment of myocardial and kidney perfusion. However, real-world registries integrating these phenotypes with clinical outcomes are lacking.

AimTo establish a registry integrating 82Rb-PET-derived myocardial and renal perfusion, CT-derived CKM imaging biomarkers, and detailed clinical and outcome data.

MethodsThe APOLLO registry is a single-centre, retrospective database comprising approximately 1,200 consecutive patients who underwent myocardial perfusion imaging with 82Rb-PET/CT at Alrijne Hospital (Leiderdorp, the Netherlands) between 2021-2023. Clinical, laboratory, medication, echocardiographic, and imaging data were retrospectively collected. Myocardial perfusion was quantified using myocardial blood flow and myocardial flow reserve, and renal perfusion using renal blood flow and effective renal plasma flow. Additional CT-derived biomarkers included measures of adiposity and frailty, great vessel diameters, and vascular calcification. Echocardiographic diastolic dysfunction grade, H2FPEF score, CKM stage, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) were also collected.

ConclusionThe APOLLO registry integrates {superscript 2}Rb-PET-derived myocardial and renal perfusion measurements with CT-derived CKM imaging biomarkers and clinical outcomes. This enables investigation of cardio-renal perfusion and their associations with CKM phenotypes and cardiovascular outcomes.

metadata.summary: Nutraceuticals such as (+)-Catechin are emerging as promising agents for the prevention and treatment of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. A large prospective study of 34,492 participants previously demonstrated an inverse association between (+)-Catechin intake and risk for coronary heart disease. Our recent work further showed that (+)-Catechin inhibits several atherosclerosis related processes in vitro, induces beneficial metabolic changes in male C57BL/6J mice fed a high fat diet (HFD), and reduces plaque burden and inflammation in male low-density lipoprotein (LDL) receptor deficient (LDLr / ) mice fed a HFD. Given known sex specific differences in atherosclerosis, it is essential to extend these investigations to female mice. The objective of this study was therefore to investigate the effects of (+)-Catechin in female LDLr /  mice in vivo. (+)-Catechin lowered plasma cholesterol levels, reduced circulating T cell populations, and increased several beneficial short chain fatty acids in both the plasma and the faeces. It also decreased plaque size, lipid content, macrophage accumulation, and CD3⁺ T cell infiltration in the aortic root, while enhancing markers of plaque stability. RNA sequencing (RNA seq) of the thoracic aorta revealed modulation of key pathways involved in inflammatory signalling, hypertension and immune responses. Complementary studies in human aortic smooth muscle cells demonstrated that (+)-Catechin attenuated macropinocytosis and oxidised LDL uptake, processes linked to plaque progression, without promoting calcification. RNA seq identified several genes and pathways consistent with the compound’s anti atherogenic and plaque stabilising actions. Collectively, these findings provide new mechanistic insights into the beneficial cardiovascular effects of (+)-Catechin in female mice and support further evaluation of this flavanol in human clinical trials.

observations.title: The antioxidant (+)-Catechin reduces inflammation and promotes a stable plaque phenotype in female LDL receptor deficient mice fed a high-fat diet via anti Inflammatory and smooth muscle cell regulatory pathways

observations.text:
BackgroundReal-world evidence on food-as-medicine programs for irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is scarce, and single-arm evaluations overstate improvement because of regression to the mean (RTM). We estimated change in the IBS Symptom Severity Scale (IBS-SSS, 0-500) in a multi-omics personalized digital health food-as-medicine program, unadjusted and RTM-corrected.

MethodsRetrospective single-arm cohort. Of 15,933 members with a valid baseline, 2,254 had a follow-up reading and 1,683 one at least 14 days after baseline. Change at 4, 12 (primary) and 26 weeks was estimated by baseline severity stratum, unadjusted and RTM-corrected by analysis of covariance. A responder fell by at least 50 points (the minimal clinically important difference benchmark). Sensitivity analyses covered equity, inverse-probability weighting and tipping-point analyses for members without a reading in each landmark window, a negative-control stratum and medication. The association of weight loss and dietary nutrient density with symptom change was evaluated within and between members.

ResultsAt 12 weeks (n = 430) IBS-SSS fell by 43.88 points unadjusted (95% confidence interval [CI] -52.44 to -35.32; p < 0.001) and by 47.73 RTM-corrected (-55.48 to -39.98; p < 0.001); 720 of 1,339 symptomatic members (53.8%; 95% CI 51.1 to 56.4) fell by at least 50 points. Larger improvement in more severe members persisted after RTM correction (severe stratum, n = 37: unadjusted -127.43, RTM-corrected -60.71, 95% CI -97.75 to -23.68, p = 0.001). A higher meal nutrient density was associated with lower IBS-SSS within a members own trajectory (p = 0.018) while weight change was not (p = 0.361). Improvement was similar across groups in spite of baseline differences by age and sex: RTM-corrected 12-week change did not differ by age (p = 0.458), body-mass index (p = 0.328), sex (p = 0.749), income (p = 0.486) or ethnicity (p = 0.170). Estimates were robust to weighting for members without a reading in the landmark window (RTM-corrected estimates moved by less than 2 points), and the change of those members would have had to be 39 to 73 points worse than observed before the mean change reached zero. Baseline medication use and starting a GLP-1 receptor agonist did not explain symptom changes.

ConclusionsIBS-SSS fell significantly among program participants, with steeper improvement in the more severe group, even after RTM correction. The improvement was comparable across socioeconomic characteristics, age and sex and robust to the confounders and missing-data assumptions evaluated. These associations from a self-selected single-arm cohort warrant replication in independent studies.
observations.title: Change in irritable bowel syndrome symptom severity among members of a multi-omic digital food-as-medicine program: a retrospective single-arm cohort study with estimates corrected for regression to the mean

metadata.summary: Background: Hypothermic oxygenated perfusion (HOPE) may extend donor heart preservation beyond conventional storage durations. We evaluated early graft function and myocardial cellular and metabolic integrity following porcine heart transplantation after 20 hours of HOPE.  Methods: Ten donor hearts underwent various preservation conditions: static cold storage (SCS) for 4 hours (n=2), HOPE for 4 hours (n=3), and HOPE for 20 hours (n=5), followed by heart transplantation (HT) in recipient pigs. Following implant and reperfusion, graft function was assessed over 3 hours by serial echocardiography, invasive hemodynamics, optical flow analysis, and vasoactive support scoring; myocardial tissue was analyzed by histopathology, flow cytometry, mitochondrial respirometry, transcriptomics, and proteomics.  Results: Ejection fraction, right atrial pressure and systolic blood pressure did not differ significantly between groups, and no graft met criteria for primary graft dysfunction. LV contractility was within normal range with comparable vasoactive support among all groups. Preservation-associated weight gain was greatest after HOPE 20h, and histopathology showed comparable findings with edema present in all cohorts, without fibrosis, thrombosis, or necrosis. Cardiomyocyte viability was preserved across all groups (HOPE 20h, 86%, HOPE 4h, 81%, and SCS 4h, 77%). Maximal oxygen consumption rate was elevated in HOPE 20h versus HOPE 4h and SCS 4h (p<0.01), while basal and non-mitochondrial respiration were similar. Transcriptomics and proteomics revealed minimal differences in gene and pathway expression among groups.   Conclusions: HOPE preserves donor heart viability, mitochondrial integrity, and ventricular function after 20 hours of ischemia in a porcine model, without evidence of primary graft dysfunction, supporting extended preservation for heart transplantation. Edema, recovery of function, and metabolic responses warrant further investigation with longer-term monitoring.

observations.title: Twenty-Hour Hypothermic Oxygenated Perfusion Preserves Myocardial Viability and Bioenergetics with No Primary Graft Dysfunction After Porcine Heart Transplantation

metadata.summary: Developing arteries must withstand pulsatile blood flow while remaining sufficiently flexible to accommodate changing hemodynamic demands. Endothelial interactions with perivascular cells and extracellular matrix are essential for this balance, but the signaling mechanisms that coordinate them remain incompletely understood. We previously showed that SH2 domain protein E (She), an endothelial adaptor protein implicated in ABL signaling, limits the size of the dorsal aorta (DA) in zebrafish embryos. Here, we investigated why zebrafish she mutants subsequently develop DA collapse and circulatory failure at 4–5 days post-fertilization. Before circulatory failure, the mutant DA retained an approximately circular cross-section and showed no detectable changes in the endothelial cell geometry, but exhibited increased distensibility during the cardiac cycle. Mutants had fewer perivascular stromal cells between the DA and posterior cardinal vein, smaller perivascular col1a1 and col5a1 expression domains, and reduced col1a1 transcript level. Single-cell RNA sequencing independently identified a reduced relative abundance of perivascular fibroblast subpopulation. In contrast, DA-associated mural cell numbers, laminin immunoreactivity, and local col4a1 transcript levels were not detectably altered. Ablation of pdgfrb-positive cells largely prevented DA narrowing and circulatory failure, while the nitric oxide donor sodium nitroprusside provided partial rescue. These findings support a contribution of mural cell-dependent vascular tone to collapse of the mechanically vulnerable DA. Mutants also exhibited cardiac chamber enlargement, increased atrial and bulbus arteriosus deformation, atrioventricular regurgitation, and increased Elastin B accumulation in the enlarged bulbus arteriosus. However, endocardial-specific She expression failed to rescue circulatory failure, supporting its requirement in vascular endothelium. Together, these findings link She function to perivascular fibroblast abundance, fibrillar collagen-gene expression, and arterial stability. They support a model in which impaired perivascular support renders the developing DA susceptible to mural cell-associated collapse, extending the role of She from early vessel-size regulation to maintenance of vascular function.

observations.title: SH2 Domain Protein E sustains perivascular fibroblasts to maintain arterial stability
